short.q: Explain why the Sahara has a very low population density.
short.model: It is extremely hot and dry with little water, so crops cannot grow and few people can survive. Soils are also thin and infertile.

short.q: Explain two push factors that make people migrate from rural areas.
short.model: Low incomes and unemployment because farms are small and droughts destroy crops. Poor services such as schools and hospitals also push families to cities.

short.q: Explain how remittances benefit a source country.
short.model: Migrants send money to their families, which raises household incomes. Families can then spend more on food, education and housing, boosting the local economy.

short.q: Explain one problem for a receiving area when many migrants arrive.
short.model: Housing, schools and hospitals can become overcrowded as demand rises faster than supply. This may lead to long waiting lists and tension in the community.

short.q: Why do refugees often move to neighbouring countries first?
short.model: Neighbouring countries are close, so travel is quick and cheap, and borders can be crossed more easily. Families often hope to return home when the conflict ends.
